title: Section separation characterizes a conservative family of points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and let $\{p_i:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of points [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For each $i$, let $u_i:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ be the functor $u_i(U)=p_i^{-1}(h_U^\#)$, where $h_U=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,U)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$, an object $U$, a section $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ and $x\in u_i(U)$, let $\tilde t:h_U^\#\to\mathcal F$ be the morphism corresponding to $t$ (the Yoneda map $h_U\to\mathcal F$, $\phi\mapsto\mathcal F(\phi)(t)$, extended through the sheafification), and write $[U,x,t]_{p_i}=p_i^{-1}(\tilde t)(x)\in p_i^{-1}\mathcal F$; this is the image of the class of the triple $(U,x,t)$ in the stalk $\varinjlim_{(U,x)}\mathcal F(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] under the canonical comparison map to $p_i^{-1}\mathcal F$. If for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$, every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, and every pair $s\ne s'$ in $\mathcal F(U)$ there are $i\in I$ and $x\in u_i(U)$ with $[U,x,s]_{p_i}\ne[U,x,s']_{p_i}$, then the inverse-image functors $p_i^{-1}$ jointly reflect isomorphisms of sheaves: whenever every $p_i^{-1}(a)$ is a bijection, a morphism $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 00YK (Definition definition-enough-points) and 00YM (Lemma lemma-enough), using the stalk identifications of Tags 00Y6 and 00Y8.

proof.text: Let $a:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism whose inverse image under every $p_i$ is a bijection. For $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ one has $a\circ\tilde t=\widetilde{a_U(t)}$: both restrict along $h_U\to h_U^\#$ to the Yoneda map of $a_U(t)$ (naturality of $a$), so they agree by the uniqueness in the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Hence $p_i^{-1}(a)([U,x,t]_{p_i})=p_i^{-1}(a\circ\tilde t)(x)=[U,x,a_U(t)]_{p_i}$. If sections $s,s'\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy $a_U(s)=a_U(s')$, then they cannot be distinct: if they were, the section-separation hypothesis would give an index $i$ and $x\in u_i(U)$ with $[U,x,s]_{p_i}\ne[U,x,s']_{p_i}$, while $p_i^{-1}(a)$ sends both to $[U,x,a_U(s)]_{p_i}=[U,x,a_U(s')]_{p_i}$, contradicting injectivity of $p_i^{-1}(a)$. Thus $a_U$ is injective for every $U$; since morphisms of sheaves are natural transformations, a morphism with injective components is a monomorphism of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: Tag 00YM (lemma-enough), converse proof: injectivity is an immediate consequence of the section-separation condition

proof.text:
Form the pushout $P=\mathcal G\amalg_{\mathcal F}\mathcal G$ in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, with coprojections $j_1,j_2:\mathcal Gightrightarrows P$: take the sectionwise pushout of presheaves of sets and sheafify; since sheafification is left adjoint to the inclusion [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps from the sheafification to a sheaf are the same as compatible pairs of maps from $\mathcal G$, so this is a pushout in sheaves. Each $p_i^{-1}$ is a left adjoint in the geometric-morphism datum [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so it carries this pushout to a pushout $p_i^{-1}P$ of $p_i^{-1}(a)$ along itself with coprojections $p_i^{-1}(j_1),p_i^{-1}(j_2)$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. A bijection is an epimorphism of sets, so by the cokernel-pair criterion [lem-galois-epi-iff-cokernel-pair] $p_i^{-1}(j_1)=p_i^{-1}(j_2)$ for every $i$. If $j_1

e j_{2,U}(g)$ in $P(U)$. The section-separation hypothesis applied to $P$ gives $i$ and $x\in u_i(U)$ with $[U,x,j_{1,U}(g)]_{p_i}
e[U,x,j_{2,U}(g)]_{p_i}$; but as in Step 1, $[U,x,j_{k,U}(g)]_{p_i}=p_i^{-1}(j_k)([U,x,g]_{p_i})$ for $k=1,2$, and these agree. Therefore $j_1=j_2$.

source.place: Tag 00YM (lemma-enough), converse proof: use the pushout $\mathcal G\amalg_{\mathcal F}\mathcal G$ and stalkwise equality of its two maps to $\mathcal G$

proof.text: The cokernel-pair characterization of epimorphisms says that a morphism is an epimorphism exactly when the two coprojections into its pushout with itself are equal. Applying it to $a$ and the pushout above, the equality $j_1=j_2$ proves that $a$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 00YM (lemma-enough), converse proof, citing Categories Lemma 08LR (lemma-characterize-mono-epi)

proof.text: We have shown that $a$ is both monic and epic. A monomorphism and epimorphism of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism by the balancedness statement for $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, namely [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sets-mono-epi-iso]. Thus every morphism whose inverse images under all $p_i$ are bijections is an isomorphism, which is exactly joint reflection of isomorphisms.

from.place: The historical proof route for pointwise conservativity: the finite-limit and finite-refinement criterion for enough points in the point-construction part of the local-term argument.

split_report.summary: Split the section-separation criterion into four steps: section separation forces injectivity on every object, the pushout coprojections are equal after using preservation of pushouts by each inverse-image left adjoint and the same separation test, the cokernel-pair criterion gives epimorphy, and the sheaf mono-plus-epi criterion gives an isomorphism. No new nodes or attachments were needed; the existing stalk-colimit identification is part of the item statement.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the historical pointwise-conservativity route in the ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality: Tags 00YK/00YM define conservative point families and prove the section-separation converse, while the stalk identifications are supplied in the item statement.
